clue.text: Amnesty International stops representative ever returning

indicators.note: the letter stops up a gap, sitting inside the other pieces like a plug
in this clue the word ever comes back the other way, read from its end

parts.note: the word ever, taken as written before being turned round

explanation.surface: The human-rights charity Amnesty International campaigns while a representative never comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amnesty International' reads as the charity, but the name splits: 'Amnesty' is the definition. 'returning' gives REVE and 'stops' plugs the I into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprieve is a pardon or cancellation of punishment, which is what an amnesty grants.

clue.text: What may indicate way finale of chorus rises

indicators.note: the finale is the closing letter of the word, the one that will be shifted
in a down clue rising means climbing nearer the top of the column, one place up

parts.note: to chorus is to sing together

explanation.surface: A singer notes how the closing note of a chorus goes up in pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finale of' and 'rises' together move the last letter of SING up one place in the down entry, so G jumps above N.
explanation.definitionFit: A road sign or signpost shows travellers which direction to take.

clue.text: Headrest has base supporting raised edge

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes last
in a down clue raising a word turns it to read from the bottom up

parts.note: a lip is an edge or rim
base can mean low, as in low or mean behaviour

explanation.surface: A headrest is described as having a base under a raised rim, like a car seat fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillow is a cushion on which a sleeper's head rests.

clue.text: Potentially hostile agents work to break secret police chief

indicators.note: the work word breaks into the chief's name, splitting it open

parts.note: Lavrentiy Beria headed Stalin's secret police, the NKVD
to act is to work or function

explanation.surface: Hostile agents set out to bring down the head of the secret police, a spy thriller plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agents' suggests spies, but here they are germs; 'to break' sends the work word into the Soviet police chief's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacteria are microbes, and some act as disease-causing organisms, so hostile only potentially.

clue.text: Leading man died during Advent

indicators.note: during means within a period, so these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: an advent is a coming or arrival
taken as written
D is the usual abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A man leading something died in the weeks before Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advent' suggests the church season but stands for COMING; 'during' places MAN+D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A commanding position or lead is one that is in front and in control.

clue.text: Drunk behaved like old youth

parts.note: behaving like something is being it, so this gives was
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth with Edwardian-style clothes

explanation.surface: Someone got drunk and acted like a youngster of old.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy (Ted) was a British teenager of the 1950s known for drape jackets and rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasted is slang for very intoxicated, a synonym of drunk.

clue.text: Lied about one possessed by spirit and passion

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of lied are moved around
possessed by means held inside the other piece

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic spirit
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone told lies about a person in the grip of drink and passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives the shuffled letters DELI, and 'possessed by' places the numeral inside the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Delirium can mean wild excitement or frenzy, close to an overwhelming passion.

clue.text: This author's support for audience is strong

indicators.note: spoken for an audience, the words are judged by what listeners hear

parts.note: this author's is my, the setter's own, and a support for a golf ball is a tee

explanation.surface: The writer says their support gives the audience strength.
explanation.walkthrough: MY TEE, the setter's golf tee, said aloud gives the answer; 'for audience' signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Mighty means powerful, a plain synonym for strong.

clue.text: Unconscionable choice of partners leading ambitious alliance?

indicators.note: here the choice word sits among the partners, so it goes between the two letter pairs
partners come as a pair, so the leading pair of letters is taken from each of the last two words

parts.note: or is the word that offers a choice

explanation.surface: An unscrupulous pairing heads an ambitious alliance of rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partners leading' takes the first two letters of 'ambitious' and 'alliance', and 'of' sets the choice word between those two pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: An unconscionable person has no conscience, and amoral describes someone lacking any moral sense.

clue.text: Club that's suitable for evening out

definitions.meaning: used for smoothing creases, that is evening out cloth

explanation.surface: A nightclub that is a good place for a night on the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evening out' suggests a night out, but it means making cloth even.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf iron is a club, and the household iron flattens and smooths fabric.

clue.text: Personal support by nameless friend is genuine

parts.note: a leg supports a person

indicators.note: N is the abbreviation for name, so a nameless word loses that letter

parts.note: an intimate is a close friend

explanation.surface: Personal backing from an anonymous friend proves real.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' removes N, the abbreviation for name, from INTIMATE, leaving ITIMATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Legitimate means lawful or authentic, the opposite of fake, so real.

clue.text: Craven Cottage finally fills lowly ground

indicators.note: fills means the letter goes inside the other piece
ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters of lowly are rearranged
finally points to the end letter of cottage

explanation.surface: Craven Cottage, Fulham FC's London football stadium, finally fills its humble ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Craven Cottage is the home of Fulham, a London football club, so 'Craven' looks like a name. 'ground' rearranges LOWLY and 'fills' puts the E there.
explanation.definitionFit: Craven means cowardly, and yellow is a slang word for cowardly.

clue.text: Distressing assessment led by doctor

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece led by another comes after it

parts.note: to doctor a drink is to lace it
a rating is an assessment

explanation.surface: A troubling evaluation is given by a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a physician but is the verb meaning to spike.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerating means wounding or harrowing, so causing great distress.

clue.text: Dreadful drone interrupts your lamentable song

indicators.note: interrupts means breaking into the middle of another word

parts.note: thy is the old form of your

indicators.note: dreadful signals that drone is in a terrible state, its letters scrambled

explanation.surface: An awful droning breaks up your mournful tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' gives the rearranged letters RENOD, and 'interrupts' splits the old word for your after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A threnody is an elegy or song of mourning, sung as a lament for the dead.

clue.text: Free variable forms part of line that's articulated

indicators.note: articulated means spoken aloud, so the answer is how the words sound

parts.note: x is the classic algebraic variable; someone who queues joins and becomes part of a line

explanation.surface: A mathematician describes a free variable that forms part of a joined-up line.
explanation.walkthrough: X and QUEUES spoken together give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone is to release or let them off a duty, so free them.

clue.text: Confident and with good reason, drinking half of Guinness

indicators.note: drinking means taking the other letters in, so they sit inside

parts.note: sane means of sound mind, thinking with reason

indicators.note: half of points to the first four letters of the eight-letter word

explanation.surface: Someone feels confident, and with good cause, after downing half a pint of stout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes the first four letters of the stout's name, and 'drinking' puts them inside the word for rational.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanguine means optimistic and positive, so hopeful and confident.

clue.text: Song in the middle of alto's range is a catchy number?

indicators.note: in means the song sits between the other letters
the middle of points to the central letters of the word

parts.note: an aria is a song from an opera

explanation.surface: A song pitched in the middle of the alto's vocal range is catchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catchy number' looks like a hit tune, but a lariat is a lasso, used to catch cattle on the range.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a rope used to catch animals, so playfully a number that catches.

clue.text: I restate how this paper could have been edited

indicators.note: editing reworks text, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An academic notes that their restated argument could have been revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could have been edited' rearranges I RESTATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written paper or essay on a subject.

clue.text: Husband's acted badly before divorce

indicators.note: before here says the jumbled piece goes in front of the husband letter
badly signals the letters of acted are jumbled

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband behaved terribly before the couple split up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' gives the scrambled letters DETAC, and 'before' puts them ahead of the husband's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To divorce two things is to separate them, which is to detach.

clue.text: Transport cafe's opening for business?

definitions.meaning: to transport is to carry away with delight, to enrapture
the door a cafe opens to customers is its way in

explanation.surface: A transport cafe, a British roadside diner for lorry drivers, opens for trade.
explanation.walkthrough: A transport cafe is a cheap British roadside eatery used by truckers; the phrase splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance is to enchant, and an entrance is a doorway or way in.

clue.text: Had to avoid bottom in deep end when swimming

indicators.note: swimming letters move about freely, so they are rearranged
in a down clue the bottom of a word is its final letter, here left out

explanation.surface: A swimmer had to keep off the bottom in the deep end of the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoid bottom in' drops P from DEEP, leaving DEE; 'when swimming' rearranges DEE+END.
explanation.definitionFit: Needed means was required to, which in the past tense is had to.

clue.text: Felt sick and unable to talk

definitions.meaning: retched, felt the urge to vomit

explanation.definitionFit: Gagging is retching, and someone with a gag over the mouth is silenced.

clue.text: Channel close to going on air

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: to air a view is to utter it

explanation.surface: A broadcasting channel is shutting down while still on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' and 'on air' suggest television, but the channel is a drain.
explanation.definitionFit: A gutter is a trough or channel that carries rainwater away.

clue.text: Establishment catering for people confusing art, nature and science primarily

indicators.note: confusing mixes the letters up so they are rearranged
primarily points to the first letter of science

explanation.surface: A debate muddles art, nature and science, chiefly to cater to people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusing' rearranges ART, NATURE and S, the first letter of science that 'primarily' picks.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant is a business that serves meals to paying diners.

clue.text: Advance payment had to include note

indicators.note: including something takes it inside, so the letter goes within

parts.note: to have a meal is to eat it, so had gives ate

explanation.surface: A deposit paid upfront has to cover an extra note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' means consumed, giving ATE; 'to include' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the ante is a stake paid before the deal, so paid in advance.

clue.text: Mass meeting to ditch right and form union

indicators.note: ditching a letter means dropping it out of the word

parts.note: a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: A mass trade meeting votes to abandon the right wing and set up a union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ditch' removes R from RALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: To ally is to join together in alliance, which is what forming a union does.

clue.text: Flag new introduction to novel containing nothing by writer

indicators.note: by means placed alongside, so the writer piece sits next to the rest

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: containing means the letters hold the zero inside
an introduction to a word is its first letter

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A flag introduces a new novel with nothing written by its author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' puts O between N (new) and N (introduction to novel), and 'by' puts PEN alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long, narrow flag or streamer, as on a lance.

clue.text: Hospital eradicating first sign of unwanted rash

indicators.note: removing the first sign of a word drops its opening letter

parts.note: something needless is unnecessary, so unwanted

explanation.surface: A hospital is wiping out the first trace of an unwanted skin rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like a skin complaint but is the adjective meaning reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedless means careless, acting without thought, which is what rash means.
